points.description: The top of the stack is the head (beginning/front) of the linked list, so push adds and pop removes elements at the head/beginning of the list.
points.partial_credit: Half or more if the student says to use a linked list with push/pop at one end but does not clearly say the head/beginning, or gives only the top-at-head idea without push/pop.

points.description: States that both push and pop operate at the same end (add/remove at the beginning), giving constant-time LIFO behaviour via a linked list.
points.partial_credit: Half if only push or only pop is described at the head.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying the stack's top is the head of the linked list and push/pop insert/remove at the beginning, in any wording. Part marks for a vague or half-correct version, e.g. a linked list with push/pop at one end without naming the head. No marks for answers about arrays, or that put push/pop at the tail or mismatched ends.
